stances.claim: The Philippines' improvement from 129th to 105th in the 2012 CPI — driven by SALN vigilance, P-Noy's transparency passion, and Ombudsman Morales's appointment — is a meaningful step but still leaves the country in the bottom third globally; continued legislative action (Whistle-blower Protection, expanded AMLA, FOI) is essential.

stances.claim: All three pending anti-corruption legislative measures — the Whistle-blower Protection Act, the expanded AMLA, and the FOI bill — should be enacted before the January 31 Gopac conference opens, to maximize the Philippines' credibility before 500 international delegates and TI chair Labelle.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban reports the Philippines' improvement in the 2012 Transparency International Corruption Perception Index -- from 129th to 105th (tied, score 34/100) -- noting it surpassed Vietnam, Indonesia, and Bangladesh but remains in the bottom third globally. He quotes retired Judge Dolores Español (TI cofounder and international advisory council member) attributing the improvement to renewed SALN vigilance, P-Noy's transparency advocacy, and the appointment of Ombudsman Morales. He situates the improvement within the broader context of the 5th Gopac International Conference to be hosted in Manila (January 31 - February 2, 2013) at the PICC -- attended by 500+ delegates from six continents, keynoted by President Aquino, and featuring TI Chair Huguette Labelle who agreed to 'feel' the Philippine anti-corruption war. The conference theme is 'Good Leaders, Good Laws, Good Citizens,' focused on UNCAC implementation and AMLA use against graft. He closes with a direct challenge to the legislature: pass all three pending anti-corruption measures -- the Whistle-blower Protection Act, the expanded AMLA covering pawnshops/forex/remittance companies, and the FOI bill (already Senate-approved, awaiting final House passage) -- before the Gopac conference opens on January 31, so the Philippines earns maximum international credibility: 'How about it, your honors?'
